caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. AT&T Mobility Services LLC
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
claims: FCRA § 1681b(b)(3)(A); ICRAA §§ 1786.40/1786.50; Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E)/(j)(4)(A); Breach of Contract; Implied Covenant; Promissory Estoppel; Negligent Misrepresentation
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT — E.D. Cal. Sacramento; seven counts. Offer, First Advantage task, and rescission are all May 28, 2026; no delayed-discovery date. Inspection demands drafted but unsigned.
note: The September 8, 2026 San Joaquin packet is historical work product only; it never reached the clerk. Generate the federal review-draft PDF with internal/scripts/matter36-edca-complaint.py. Unsigned inspection demands: internal/docs/matter-36/INSPECTION_DEMAND_FIRST_ADVANTAGE.md and PERSONNEL_FILE_DEMAND_ATT.md. Do not plead May 29, 2026. Serve the current SOS agent, not 2439 W. Kettleman Lane. Confirm the Mobility Services LLC listing before service; do not invent CSC. First Advantage is not a named defendant. Do not treat another employer's report as AT&T's report.
defendants: AT&T Mobility Services LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report and party to the May 28, 2026 written offer. AT&T Inc. is not named merely as parent. First Advantage Background Services Corp. is pleaded as AT&T's CRA from the May 28, 10:19 a.m. task (AT&T Non Management, account 132156) and remains a nonparty discovery source unless AT&T-specific records support an independent CRA claim. Richard Patterson and Orville R. Bell are witnesses, not presently named.
causes: [FEDERAL ANCHOR] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — AT&T allegedly took adverse employment action based in whole or in part on the First Advantage report or screening process without first providing the report and written Summary of Rights; negligent/willful remedies under §§ 1681o/1681n. Timely from May 28, 2026. No delayed-discovery date.

[DISTINCT STATE OMISSION] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — upon denying employment under circumstances in which an investigative report was obtained, AT&T allegedly failed to advise Plaintiff and supply the CRA name/address at adverse action. The 10:19 a.m. task is not the § 1786.40 advice. Pleaded as a different omission from the FCRA pre-adverse failure.

[I&B ULTIMATE FACTS] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — complaint pleads on information and belief that First Advantage furnished Plaintiff's California-registry information and AT&T used it in reversing the accepted Lodi offer, supported by the two-hour sequence, named vendor, contemporaneous Megan's Law listing, and UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparators. CCP § 338(a) from May 28, 2026 use → May 28, 2029. Exact source-field wording reserved for discovery.

[INDEPENDENT PATH] Breach of written contract — official offer with price, worksite, manager, and June 15 start; Plaintiff accepted through Workday and began onboarding; Spanish was not a listed contingency.
[INDEPENDENT PATH] Implied covenant — using a closed Spanish window or a two-hour CRA sequence to gut the bargain.
[ALTERNATIVE] Promissory estoppel — if no contract, the same writing still induced reliance.
[INDEPENDENT PATH] Negligent misrepresentation — official bilingual offer after the ACTFL window closed on May 25.
[OMITTED] UCL — limited remedial upside and unnecessary federal standing/remedy side fight.
[OMITTED] CCRAA — reserve unless the actual AT&T product is an ordinary consumer credit report rather than an investigative employment report.

[RESERVED] Intentional fraud/concealment, FCRA § 1681b(b)(2)(A), Fair Chance / FEHA, and First Advantage vendor claims — add only if internal proof, the authorization package, CRD exhaustion, or CRA conduct support them. Do not plead § 1332 with invented LLC members.
key_facts: On May 16, 2026, Plaintiff submitted two AT&T applications: R-107776 Retail Sales Consultant at Stockton Pacific and R-106742 Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant at Lodi. Both advanced through interviews. LTI provided an ACTFL Telephone OPIc Spanish test expiring May 25; the record still lacks the score, audio, threshold, receipt time, and decision notes. On May 28 at 10:13 a.m., Workday officially offered R-106742: Retail Sales Consultant reporting to Orville R. Bell at 2439 W. Kettleman Lane, $24.95/hour paid biweekly, $13,700 annual target variable compensation prorated for part-time hours, tentative June 15 start, candidate C-1690172. Contingencies omit Spanish. Workday issued onboarding tasks at 10:15–10:17 a.m.; First Advantage sent the AT&T Non Management screening task (account 132156) at 10:19 a.m. At 12:23 p.m., Patterson texted that the manager no longer wanted to proceed because Plaintiff did not pass Spanish. Plaintiff accepted through Workday, began onboarding, and received no pre-adverse report or rights summary. Report contents and use are I&B ultimate facts. No count uses a delayed-discovery date.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal redraft. The signed San Joaquin complaint dated September 8, 2026 was never clerk-filed. Proposed forum is E.D. Cal. Sacramento (L.R. 120(d)). Serve the current SOS agent, not the Lodi store; confirm the Mobility Services LLC listing and do not invent CSC. Unsigned §§ 1786.22 / 1198.5 demands are drafted. No count pleads May 29, 2026. Count 3 is timely under CCP § 338(a) from the May 28, 2026 use (outer bound May 28, 2029). Remaining gates: Plaintiff signature, official JS-44 / AO-440, SOS-agent confirmation, sending the inspection demands, and a final hostile audit of every I&B allegation.
damages: The offer confirms $24.95/hour, biweekly pay, a $13,700 annual variable-compensation target prorated for part-time hours, and a tentative June 15, 2026 start. It does not state weekly hours; those figures are not invented. Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual/compensatory damages according to proof; FCRA remedies under §§ 1681n/1681o; ICRAA actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater; Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) remedies; and contract/estoppel expectation or reliance damages. Portfolio valuation remains the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $90,000 / $135,000 / $175,000. Do not plead § 1332 amount-in-controversy on invented LLC citizenship.
risk: Strongest of the four San Joaquin packets on paper: written offer, $24.95, start date, two-hour rescission, confirmed Workday acceptance, and a named vendor that is not a defendant. If production shows no report before 12:23, Counts 1–3 thin out; contract, covenant, estoppel, and misrepresentation still stand. Do not plead May 29 — the events are May 28, and a next-day discovery date would look like gamesmanship. Do not plead § 1332. Confirm SOS before service. If the AT&T report later shows ordinary court records and no California-registry source, drop or recast § 290.46 and keep FCRA/ICRAA/contract. Plaintiff’s reply to Patterson is not a waiver. Do not concede the Spanish failure.
